subject: science
intro: Hi, I'm Mr. Patel, 6th grade science. Let's plan a lesson on the water cycle that goes beyond the textbook diagram.

beats.narration: I title lessons with a phenomenon question students can relate to.
beats.text: Where Does the Puddle Go? The Water Cycle

beats.narration: This standard asks students to model the cycling of water driven by sunlight and gravity.
The key idea is the energy source, which the textbook diagram usually leaves out.
beats.text: Students will be able to develop a model showing how water changes state and moves through the water cycle, and identify the energy source driving each process.

beats.narration: Their first ideas become a baseline we come back to at the end.
beats.text: Show a time-lapse of a puddle disappearing on a sunny day. Students write where they think the water went.

beats.narration: The demo shows condensation and "rain" happening on their desks.
beats.text: Walk through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, labeling each with its energy source: the sun heats the water, and gravity pulls it back down. Demo: a bowl of hot water covered with plastic wrap and ice on top.

beats.narration: The bags keep running all week, so they can watch the cycle over several days.
beats.text: Groups build a water cycle model in a zip bag taped to the window and draw it, labeling each process and whether energy is added or released.

beats.narration: Revising their own first idea shows growth clearly.
beats.text: Revise your answer to "Where did the puddle go?" using at least three water cycle terms.

outro: Phenomenon, model, revise. That's the arc. Now you try.
